transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Everleaf Head of Search), Connor (Everleaf Staff Eng), Aisha (Everleaf PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, brief):
Everleaf is evaluating a hosted path for embeddings + rerank to improve search relevance and down-cost pipeline operations. Primary goals: improve top-3 precision, reduce tail latency, and simplify ops vs their current Elastic + custom ANN layer. Key asks: security (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), cost at 3M queries/mo, and a short POC to validate recall + latency.

Topics: hosted embeddings endpoint, reranking endpoint (cross-encoder), candidate retrieval patterns, console demo, Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/caching), security posture, pricing and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Maya Thompson from Redwood, AE on the commerce vertical. With me is Diego, our SE, he'll do the walkthrough. Priya, great to meet you — and Connor, Aisha, hi!

[00:17] Priya: Thanks, Maya. Quick intro — I'm Priya, Head of Search at Everleaf. We're reworking product search, currently on Elastic + a homegrown ANN for vectors, but relevance for long-tail queries is rough and ops is heavy.

[00:36] Diego: Yep, hi, team — Diego Alvarez. We'll focus today on our hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints and show a couple of console flows. We'll also cover security and what a short POC looks like.

[00:52] Connor: Quick note — we get about 3 million search queries a month, peak QPS around 45, average session length short but tail latency annoying. We care about p95 under 300ms for search front-end.

[01:12] Maya: Perfect. Does everyone have the deck link I tossed in calendar? I'll repost in chat. Also — are there other stakeholders we should loop in for the POC?

[01:30] Priya: Yes, please add our infra lead (Elliot) and security (Marcos). They'll need SOC 2 + SAML details.

[01:45] Diego: Noted. I'll include our SOC2 report, SAML SSO doc, and KMS integration notes.

[02:02] Aisha: From product side, our success metric is top-3 relevance improvement on admin-defined queries and no regression on commerce-critical categories. Timeline: POC in April if we like results.

[02:20] Diego: Great. Let's jump into architecture. At a high level, for hosted flow we recommend: 1) embed corpus via embeddings endpoint, 2) store vectors in your chosen vector DB or Redwood-managed index, 3) candidate retrieve with ANN, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint (cross-encoder) to re-score top-N. We can also host both the index and reranker in our Hosted offering to reduce glue code.

[02:50] [screen share starts] Diego: Here's a sample curl for embeddings — note we support batching, and payloads are gzipped. Example: POST /v1/embeddings with 128 documents returns 768-d vectors (model).
